Backpressure in a streaming pipeline is the mechanism by which a slow downstream consumer signals an upstream producer to reduce its emission rate, rather than letting an unbounded buffer grow until the process runs out of memory.

## Implementations

### Bounded Queues

The producer blocks once the queue reaches capacity, preventing unbounded memory accumulation. This is a simple but synchronous approach that directly couples producer and consumer pacing.

### Credit-Based Flow Control

The consumer explicitly grants the producer permission to send N more items. This approach decouples producer and consumer to some degree while maintaining a bounded buffer through a permit/credit system.

### Reactive-Pull Models

The consumer requests items on its own schedule instead of the producer pushing items. This model inverts the control flow, allowing the consumer to pull at its own pace without the producer needing to block or maintain state about consumer readiness.
